performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body: # hand-written by @matthewhammer Hey reviewers, as I'm playing with examples that have errors in the `expand` function, I see duplicated error messages for the same line. I asked Claude about it, and got some insights; I asked Claude to post them here, and eventually got the text below, after some massaging. I thought I'd add this preface to explain it with more context. # Generated through @matthewhammer + Claude A livelit use is always wrapped in a projector, and transparent wrappers restate the marks of the term they wrap, so every expansion error gets reported twice — the mechanism isn't livelit-specific (`(y)` reports its free variable twice, `((y))` three times), it's just guaranteed to bite for livelits. The cheap fix is at the collection layer: collapse each chain of ids sharing a mark list into a single row, reported at the innermost id, promoted to the innermost *visible* wrapper when the marked term sits under a projector and so has no measurement of its own. The alternative is to stop propagating marks through wrappers in `Statics`, which is cleaner in principle but would take the projector's error decoration with it, so it's worth deciding which layer this belongs in.

To keep this PR's scope on expansion typing, the dedup fix lives in #2489, which branches off this one rather than being folded in — parked there until reviewers have a view on which layer it belongs in (collection vs. `Statics`). Nothing here changes.

One clarification on the screenshot above: it's a local edit to the emotion slide's `expand` (returning `(word(m), 1)` against `type Expansion = String`), not the slide as committed — the committed slide is clean, so reproducing the duplication needs that edit, or any error inside parens.

> It seems like expand being typed `Model -> Expand` could just be typed at livelit definition. I understand why this isn't the case in the papers quoted version.

Yeah, I guess without splices, there's a chance to do something really different from the paper here and more eager/local, in terms of typing.

But to be most like the paper, for when we do have splices, the current PR is delaying the check.

I think that's what Cyrus is asking for, but I'm not certain.

Now that I'm further reading the code I have a slightly more nuanced take. We're using the static type of the expand function to determine whether or not the expansion type is correct at invocation. The livelit paper since it returns the quoted version is relying on the output of the dynamics of the expansion function to do the invocation typechecking. I think this is probably more consequential to this design being reused for the splice version. In the screenshot above I changed the static type of the expand function to be `?` then returned an incompatible type. Because statically it's unknown it's not giving an error even though the value is `8` dynamically and clearly incompatible with the expansion type.
